source_state: uncommitted implementation; explicit managed host payload facts, constant/edge padding bounds and first-use rotary storage for external embeddings

native_runtime.patches: safemlx-sys/src/mlx-c/patches at the recorded source revision

coverage.qwen_dimensions: batch two, two layers (gated delta and ordinary attention), width 64, vocabulary 37, dense/affine-4-bit, tied/untied
coverage.sequence: warm two-token prefix; seven prompt tokens in chunks 1/3/7 with state-only/final-position/sequence demand; three cached decodes
coverage.interpretation: Dense equation spans have complete tensor and host bounds; packed projections and embeddings remain unknown. These are metadata equation results, not whole-request enforcement or new released-checkpoint measurements.

host_derivation: Audited operation names and formats are explicitly recognized after sharing tensor descriptor validation; a future tensor implementation does not automatically receive zero host workspace.

Native array initialization, copies including CPU compaction, casts, reductions, dense products, convolution, constant/edge padding and pointwise intermediates use the shared Metal allocator. Their mappings do not add a second host payload allocation.
Borrowed input slices to tensor constructors remain the responsibility of separately priced request preparation. Scalar validation results map retained native arrays directly.

Rotary construction charges all Rust F32 frequency vectors: two for native YaRN, one more for its InputProducts realization, one for proportional, or one for default/linear InputProducts. Native frequency copies remain separate.

InputScores attention with more than 8192 keys uses one query and at most 256 keys per completed accumulator call. Its local boolean payload is at most 256 bytes and is dropped before the next call. Sliding tiles may use less.
Runtime/driver and shape metadata, handle lists, JIT programs, allocator bookkeeping/cache and unrelated process memory remain outside managed payload bounds.
padding_derivation: Constant padding fills one native output, copies arbitrary input strides directly into an output alias and includes the default integer scalar and dtype conversion.

Edge padding creates zeros and an input slice-update, then at most two more full-size updates per padded axis. All copies remain charged without relying on donation. Edge slices and broadcasts share those preceding allocations.
Malformed/shrinking geometry and extension of an empty edge axis cannot receive a bound.
rotary_correction: Frequency construction storage is included before the offset/external-embedding branch, preserving first-use allocations when forward consumes supplied cosine and sine tensors.
limitations: Complete native request composition and production reservation wiring remain unfinished.
Other native formats, routing/hyper/collective mechanisms and other cache strategies still need their exact facts and enclosing resource accounting.
The native machine cannot validate newer-GPU NAX execution; its source-derived bounds are retained.
No additional pinned released-checkpoint or process-memory measurement is made in this phase.

padding_measurement.method: Evaluate and retain input, synchronize, reset peak against active baseline, pad/evaluate/synchronize, then compare incremental peak with the cold tensor bound. Host export and full independent coordinate oracle comparisons follow the peak capture. Allocator cache remains populated.
